title: Madd 'aarid lis-sukoon: the madd when we stop: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Summer 1: Al-Baqarah 285 to 286; madd laazim and 'aarid
source: Written for quran/y4 lesson 32 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Madd 'aarid lis-sukoon rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 32. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Madd 'aarid lis-sukoon
points: A madd letter, then the last letter of the word
When we stop, the last letter gets a sukoon
Hold the madd for 2, 4 or 6 counts: choose one and keep it

blocks.h: Examples at the ends of ayat

arabic.text: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ (١) ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ (٢) ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ (٣) مَٰلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ (٤)

head: Not this
This
rows: Six counts on ٱلرَّحِيمِ, then two on ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
Choose one length and keep it the same at every stop

keywords.def: lengthening a sound by a set number of counts
temporary: it appears because we stop

questions.q: Read Al-Fatihah 1:5 to 7 stopping at each ayah, with four counts every time.
questions.a: nasta'eeen, al-mustaqeeem, ad-daalleen held evenly at the stops.

questions.q: Pupil PDF: circle the madd 'aarid at the end of each ayah of Al-Fatihah and Al-Fajr 89:27 to 30. Today's rota group recites Al-Fajr 19 to 24.
questions.a: Al-Fatihah: the yaa before the last letter at the end of every ayah (ٱلرَّحِيمِ, ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ, ٱلدِّينِ, نَسْتَعِينُ, ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ); in 1:7 «ٱلضَّآلِّينَ» also ends with an 'aarid on the yaa.

questions.q: Extend: find the madd 'aarid at the ends of the ayat of An-Nas.
questions.a: Every ayah ends in «ٱلنَّاسِ» or «ٱلْخَنَّاسِ»: the alif before the last letter is 'aarid at the stop.

questions.q: Stretch: which three lengths are allowed and why must we choose one?
questions.a: 2, 4 or 6; consistency keeps the recitation even.

options: When we stop and the last letter becomes sakin
When a shaddah comes after the madd
questions.a: A) When we stop and the last letter becomes sakin. It is temporary: it appears only because of the stop.

questions.q: Stopping on «ٱلْمَصِيرُ» we can hold the yaa for ...
Think again: When we read «ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ» joined to the next ayah, the yaa is short. Why does it grow when we stop?
questions.a: Stopping puts a sukoon on the last letter, so the madd before it becomes 'aarid: 2, 4 or 6 counts.
